tool.name: Focaloop VariationLoop
tool.description: call genomic variants (SNVs and indels) from FASTQ, BAM, indexed CRAM, or Logan unitigs

tool.help:
**What this tool does**
**Focaloop VariationLoop** calls single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and small insertions or deletions (indels) for any organism with a reference genome FASTA. It avoids writing large intermediate BAM files by streaming reads directly into a low-memory pileup and duplicate-removal engine, and supports targeted CRAM slicing as well as on-the-fly removal of host or off-target reads before alignment.
-----
**How it works**
1. **Input retrieval and optional pre-filtering:** Depending on the workflow you choose, VariationLoop either aligns paired-end FASTQ reads directly, slices only the compressed CRAM blocks overlapping your BED target intervals (using the `.crai` index so unrequested regions are never read), or discards host and off-target read pairs in memory using a fast 31-mer target screen before alignment. 2. **Single-pass pileup and duplicate removal:** Aligned reads are accumulated directly into contig-level pileups with PCR duplicate filtering scaled automatically to your reference genome size. 3. **Diploid genotyping and local haplotype reassembly:** Sites passing mapping and base-quality filters are genotyped (`0/1`, `1/1`, `1/2`), and active regions containing indels, soft-clipped reads, or clustered substitutions are reassembled locally to sharpen indel coordinates and allele counts. 4. **Reporting and state export:** Results are written as a standard VCF file, a clean tabular variant summary, a self-contained HTML report, and a compact `.focaloop.tar.zst` state bundle.
**Local Galaxy History files vs. remote URLs and public accessions**
- **Galaxy History FASTQ, BAM, or CRAM files:** Processed directly from Galaxy storage with no network downloads. When you supply a CRAM file with a `.crai` index and a BED file in **Indexed CRAM region slicing** mode, only the compressed blocks overlapping your target intervals are decoded. - **Remote CRAM URLs with a `.crai` index:** Only the header and the compressed byte ranges covering your padded BED intervals are fetched over HTTPS, avoiding multi-gigabyte whole-file downloads. - **Remote FASTQ URLs or public SRA/ENA accessions:** Retrieved per sample in a manifest and aligned (or pre-filtered against your reference/BED target regions first in target-filtered mode).
**What is saved in the state bundle**
The `.focaloop.tar.zst` archive stores per-sample variant calls, alignment run statistics, and sample group metadata from your manifest. When you analyze a multi-sample cohort containing two or more labeled groups (such as two populations, sampling sites, or treatment arms), you can pass this state bundle directly to **Focaloop Query** to compare allele frequencies and compute population differentiation (Fst) in seconds with zero re-alignment.
-----
**Choosing a workflow**
| Your goal | Workflow to choose | Best inputs | |---|---|---| | Standard SNV and indel calling across a genome or gene panel | **Whole-genome or targeted variant calling** | Paired FASTQ files, aligned BAM/CRAM, or a multi-sample manifest | | Ultra-fast calling on public SRA runs without downloading raw FASTQs | **Public SRA Logan unitigs** | One or more public SRA/ENA accessions (or a cohort manifest) + reference genome | | Fast variant calling inside specific genes from large CRAM files | **Indexed CRAM region slicing** | CRAM file (History or HTTPS URL) + `.crai` index + BED target regions | | Call variants in microbial, viral, or targeted samples contaminated with host DNA | **Target-filtered FASTQ calling** | Paired FASTQ files or manifest + reference genome (or BED intervals under 45 Mb) |
-----
**Inputs and manifest format**
Choose your **Reference genome source** from a built-in Galaxy genome (CVMFS cache, default), a FASTA dataset in your Galaxy History, or an NCBI assembly accession (`GCF_` or `GCA_` prefix) downloaded automatically. Note that raw FASTQ inputs must be paired-end (R1 and R2), whereas **Public SRA Logan unitigs** streams compact pre-assembled 31-mer unitigs directly from the public Logan archive with depth-adaptive abundance filtering and optional 15-mer host removal.
For single-sample runs, select your paired FASTQ files or aligned BAM/CRAM directly from your Galaxy History. For multi-sample or remote cohorts, upload a tab-separated (TSV) or comma-separated (CSV) manifest with a header row:
| Column | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `sample_id` | Yes | Unique sample name written to VCF and summary outputs | | `group` (or `population`, `country_or_group`) | Recommended | Cohort, site, or population label used for summaries and **Focaloop Query** comparisons | | `source` (or `run_or_url`, `source_uri_or_srr`) | Yes | Local dataset stem, remote CRAM/FASTQ HTTPS URL, or public SRA/ENA accession (`SRR`, `ERR`, or `DRR` prefix) | | `mate2_url` | Remote paired FASTQ | Required HTTPS URL of the reverse (R2) FASTQ file whenever `source` is a remote R1 FASTQ URL | | `crai_uri` | Remote CRAM | HTTPS URL or path to the `.crai` index matching a remote CRAM file |
Example manifest for **Indexed CRAM region slicing**:
``` sample_id group source crai_uri sample_1 site_north https://example.org/cram/sample_1.cram https://example.org/cram/sample_1.cram.crai sample_2 site_south https://example.org/cram/sample_2.cram https://example.org/cram/sample_2.cram.crai ```
Example manifest for **Whole-genome** or **Target-filtered FASTQ calling**:
``` sample_id group source mate2_url sample_1 group_a RUN_ACCESSION_1 sample_2 group_b https://example.org/reads/sample_2_R1.fastq.gz https://example.org/reads/sample_2_R2.fastq.gz ```
-----
**Key parameters**
- **Target regions (BED):** Limits CRAM slicing, 31-mer read pre-filtering, and variant calling to specific chromosomes or intervals. Recommended whenever analyzing targeted panels or slicing large CRAM archives. - **Filter out host and off-target reads before alignment:** Available in **Target-filtered FASTQ calling**. Keeps only read pairs sharing 31-mer sequence matches with your reference or BED intervals before mapping. For genomes larger than 45 Mb, supply a target BED file covering your regions of interest (under 45 Mb total) or turn the pre-filter off. - **Read subsampling fraction:** Set below `1.0` (for example, `0.5`) to deterministically downsample deep paired-end FASTQ libraries before alignment. - **Local haplotype reassembly:** Enabled by default. Substantially improves indel accuracy and multi-nucleotide variant calls around repeat or complex regions. - **Minimum MAPQ, base quality, and QUAL thresholds:** Standard quality filters excluding low-confidence alignments, low-quality bases, and weak variant calls.
-----
**Outputs**
1. **Variant calls (`variants.vcf`):** Standard VCFv4.2 file with per-sample genotype fields (`GT:GQ:DP:AD`). Multi-sample cohorts are merged into a single VCF. 2. **Variant summary table (`variants_summary.tsv`):** Flat tab-separated table with one row per sample-variant call. 3. **HTML report:** Self-contained visual summary showing per-sample read counts, duplicate removal, SNV and indel totals, and variant distributions. 4. **State bundle (`variationloop_state.focaloop.tar.zst`):** Saved cohort archive compatible with **Focaloop Query** for follow-up population allele-frequency and Fst comparisons.
Key columns in `variants_summary.tsv`:
| Column | Meaning | |---|---| | `sample_id` | Sample identifier from your form or manifest | | `chrom`, `pos` | Reference chromosome/contig and 1-based genomic coordinate | | `ref`, `alt` | Reference allele and called alternate allele | | `kind` | Variant class (`SNV` or `INDEL`) | | `gt`, `gq` | Called genotype (`0/1` heterozygous, `1/1` homozygous alternate) and genotype quality | | `dp`, `ad_ref`, `ad_alt` | Total filtered read depth and allele depths supporting reference vs. alternate | | `qual` | Phred-scaled variant call confidence score | | `source` | Variant caller label (`variationloop`) |
-----
**Tips and troubleshooting**
- **Target pre-filter limit exceeded on a large genome:** The in-memory 31-mer host/off-target filter supports target spans up to 45 Mb. For mammalian or large plant genomes, either supply a gene-panel BED file or use **Whole-genome or targeted variant calling**. - **Matching local Galaxy History FASTQ files to a manifest:** Name paired datasets as `<sample_id>_R1.fastq.gz` and `<sample_id>_R2.fastq.gz` (or `_1` / `_2`). Trailing mate suffixes and FASTQ extensions are stripped to match `sample_id` in the manifest. - **Missing CRAM index:** Galaxy generates `.crai` indexes automatically for CRAM datasets in your History. For remote CRAM URLs, include the `.crai` URL in the `crai_uri` manifest column.
